In case anyone is wondering why files were not recognized in windows:

it is because with a "fast-boot" shutdown, apparently the entire drive contents are arranged in a super-special (retarded) way, and the autistic windows10 can't fathom having a single bit be different on the next boot than what it was expecting.

So when I copied files to the windows10 drive after a fast-boot shutdown, the file system didn't know how to handle those bits.

One created directory was "in the middle" of the fast-boot arrangement, and that was the orphaned files (all 50gb of it) but the majority of the files put at the end were allowed to be seen as real files. Since there is no way to predict where files will be placed in relation to what fast-boot has set up, it was more of a randomness to what survived. The fact that the drive was 90% empty probably helped those files survive. If the drive had 50% usage or more, I would doubt any files would survive.
